name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes where other upscalers blur edges or lose depth, giving a measurable quality bump without extra compute cost. The trade-off is that it only works on still frames—video sequences need extra stitching work later.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—faces blur worse under motion because depth maps can’t track micro-expressions. Instead, test RealVisXL’s face model with a 10-frame burst sample: if face sharpness holds across motion, it’s worth the vendor lock; if not, drop it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s face-preserving upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline *only* on the face. Faces are the highest-value target—viewers notice blur there first, and RealVisXL’s model locks onto facial features better than depth-aware upscalers under motion. The trade-off is vendor lock: RealVisXL’s model won’t help with backgrounds or non-face objects, so we accept a partial solution to maximize the most visible quality gain.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL locks us into a single vendor’s face tech—if Anthropic drifts or prices spike, we’re stuck. Test InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler on faces first: if face sharpness holds across motion, it’s vendor-neutral; if not, we accept the lock only after proving it’s the best option.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Add GFPGAN 2.0 GPU face enhancer to EXCAVA’s pipeline for face regions only—faces must stay sharp across motion, else drop it. Torque owns the A/B test against RealVisXL’s face model, proving vendor-neutral superiority or accepting lock-in only if it wins.
